experiment: Sub-04 zero-support transfer of an EEG category posterior to external H14 photo anchors. Development study. No official test EEG, stimulus, classification scores or render outcomes enter this experiment.
split: Use the original 884 physical calibration objects for fitting and the existing fixed 64+64 new classes for calibration and final evaluation. Each class has ten distinct photos, each using four original repeats. Both 64 groups were used in previous experiments for other hypotheses.
novel_element: Earlier soft_class_residual used text-only posteriors, text-synthesized means and a replacement within-class readout. Here retain the current global-angle EEG direction and use the full joint32 posterior to add an independently photographed, visually calibrated category component at the same native angle.
collision_control: Cross all 1854 external anchors with all 1280 generic calibration and validation originals by source bytes, RGB128 thumbnail and existing whole/center pHash-dHash rule before fitting. Replace flagged anchor image vectors everywhere with training-only text-synthesized image centroids so all 1854 names remain eligible. The original reference audit covers official images separately. The generic originals are opened only by this isolated collision audit and by feature scoring.
posterior: Freeze the original weighted 32-dimensional classifier. Temperature is the minimizer of full-1854-label negative log likelihood on 64 calibration objects with bounds [0.15,4]. Inference uses only EEG and the full bank, with no shortlist, truth or target image.
external_bank: Regularized kernel ridge on 884 calibration object pairs maps an external reference photo to a THINGS-EEG photo centroid. Use 50/50 linear/cubic unit cosine kernel, ridge 0.5 and leave-one-class-out PRESS correction for fitted entries. The anchor bank is 0.8 calibrated visual prototype plus 0.2 external image, unit normalized.
intervention: For each query compute the posterior-weighted bank vector. Log-map around the 884-class visual mean direction and subtract the average predicted prior log-vector on calibration. Scale the centered prior so its median norm on calibration equals the current global-angle log-vector median. Add beta times this class component to the global-angle query tangent, then renormalize to the recipient's original global angle. EEG residual denotes this full continuous query term and may encode object as well as image information.
weight_selection: Among positive beta 0.25,0.5,1.0, choose the largest mean of object64 and within10 top-one fractions on 640 calibration photos, breaking ties by all640 photo hits, then smaller beta. Always score the incumbent separately. Nothing else changes on validation.
controls: Incumbent global angle; category prior in isolation; candidate with category component exchanged to an unrelated donor object (shift by 17 entire classes keeping photo ordinal); candidate with continuous direction exchanged to a different photo within the true object (cyclic +1 within each block), holding the recipient's prior and angle. Both permutations are scoring-only controls constructed after freezing matched conditions.
endpoints: Primary object64 uses the mean of the other nine gallery images in each candidate category, leaving the query ordinal out of all 64 centroids. Each query additionally ranks all 640 original photos and its own ten. Measure single-query within-class pairwise wins, raw target cosine, true word top1/top5 among all 1854 H14 text vectors and a scoring-only 64-word menu. Report full EEG posterior NLL, ECE, precision by confidence quintile and matched-control differences on held-out classes. All queries scored regardless of word correctness.
gate: Advance to a rendering pilot only if matched minus global object64 lower paired class-bootstrap 95% bound >0, within10 and all640 top-one point differences >=0, and matched beats wrong class prior on object64 and matched beats same-object wrong EEG on within10 by positive lower 95% bounds. Bootstrap 10000 paired draws of the 64 whole objects, seed 260550, marginal intervals. Single-person exploratory data. No tuning after seeing validation.
publications: Private diagnostic. Official test and JPEG generation require a separate decision.
